name: chip
title: Chip
description: A value the reader has added — a recipient, a selected filter, a tag on a record — shown with a control to remove it.

base.summary: An outlined value, drawn with the secondary role so it reads as something the reader can act on rather than as a status. That is the visible difference from a neutral Badge, which is a filled label that nobody removes.

tokens.padding-inline-end: space.1 — the remove control sits in the end padding's place
tokens.border-radius: radius.element — documented as the radius for chips
tokens.max-inline-size: 100% of its container, with the text truncated by an ellipsis — the full value stays the remove control's name and the chip's title

remove.summary: The one interactive part. Visibly small, with a hit area stretched to the chip's full block size and past its end.

tokens.hit area: size.target.min in both dimensions, centred on the visible remove circle with a pseudo-element; the circle itself stays small so the chip stays a chip
tokens.focus ring: theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible

behavior.summary: A `<span>` holding the value's text and a `<button type="button">` that removes it. No primitive: the only behaviour is one button, and Button's activation already owns it.

decisions.decision: One component, and it is the input chip — the other four chips are already here
decisions.why: 'Chip' names five things that share a pill shape and differ in semantics, which is this system's test for splitting. A filter chip is a pressed toggle — a row of them is ToggleButtonGroup with `selectionMode="multiple"` and `attached={false}`, announced with `aria-pressed`. A choice chip is one answer from a few — SegmentedControl, or ToggleButtonGroup in single mode, announced as a radio group. A static tag is a label nobody acts on — Badge. An assist or suggestion chip is an action — a small secondary Button. The one thing left is a value the reader added and can take away, which is text plus a removal command, and no existing component is that. Shipping a `Chip` with a `kind` prop over all five would put a radiogroup, a toggle, a label, a button and a removable value behind one name, and the prop would be choosing the ARIA pattern — exactly the mistake Tabs and SegmentedControl were split to avoid.

A chip that cannot be removed is a Badge. Making the handler optional would make this a second way to draw a static label, and the two would drift; requiring it means reaching for this component is itself the statement that the value is removable.

decisions.decision: The chip is not focusable — its remove button is
decisions.why: There is one thing to do with a chip, so there is one tab stop: the button. A focusable chip around a focusable button would be two stops for one action, and a focusable chip with no button would need a keyboard command nobody could discover. The button's name is the full phrase, so focusing it says both what the value is and what will happen.

decisions.decision: The remove button is named after the value
decisions.why: Five buttons called 'Remove' tell a screen-reader user nothing about which recipient each one removes. The default name is 'Remove' followed by the chip's text — 'Remove Ada Lovelace' — and `removeLabel` replaces the whole phrase, rather than a prefix, so a translation can put the words in its own order.

decisions.decision: Backspace and Delete on the focused remove button also remove
decisions.why: Enter and Space activate it because it is a button. Backspace and Delete are what a reader expects to remove a selected value in every token field they have used, and on native platforms 'delete' is the standard accessibility action for exactly this. Accepting them costs nothing and removes a moment of 'how do I get rid of this'.

decisions.decision: Focus after removal is the caller's, until a multi-value field exists
decisions.why: Removing the chip removes the focused button, and a browser whose focused element disappears sends focus to `<body>` — a keyboard user is thrown to the top of the page. This component cannot fix that alone: only something that holds all the chips knows that the next one, or the input they were typed into, is where focus should go. So the obligation is stated on `onRemove`: move focus before or as you remove. The real fix is a multi-value field — a text input with its chips, roving focus between them, and Backspace in an empty input removing the last one — which this system does not have and which needs its own gate 1.

decisions.decision: Long values truncate, and the full value stays reachable
decisions.why: An email address can be wider than a phone. The text truncates with an ellipsis at the container's width, which is the one place truncation is acceptable: the full value is still the remove button's name and the chip's `title`, so a screen reader and a long-press both have it. Text's contract declined line clamping in general precisely because truncated text needs that second path, and here it already exists.

The hit area is size.target.min, 48px, on every platform — Material's minimum, which also clears Apple's 44pt and WCAG 2.5.5. It sizes where the control can be tapped, never the drawn box. Settled by the token interview (docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md).

On the web it renders `<span>` with the text and `<button type="button" aria-label="Remove …">` holding an `aria-hidden` glyph, with `aria-disabled` on the button when disabled. A set of chips is the caller's `<ul role="list">` with one per `<li>`, so the count is announced. On React Native it renders a `View` with `accessible`, `accessibilityLabel` set to the value, and `accessibilityActions={[{ name: "delete", label: removeLabel }]}` handled by `onAccessibilityAction` — one focus stop with the platform's own delete action, which is the native idiom and the reason the web needs a separate button and native does not. The visible remove `Pressable` is then `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` / `accessibilityElementsHidden`, so it is a touch target and not a second stop. `className` is web-only; no prop is native-only. There is no gesture: removal is always a press. Rata-drawn (decision N5): neither platform's OS controls include an input chip, so it is drawn from the same recipe; the delete action is the OS accessibility action. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).

use: A recipient's name or address, a filter's value, a tag.
dont: Markup. The text is reused in the remove button's name and the `title`, so it is a string rather than a ReactNode.
children.a11y: Read as plain text, and appended to the remove button's default name.

onRemove.summary: Called when the reader removes the value — by pressing the button, or by Backspace or Delete while it has focus.
use: Removing the value from the caller's state, and moving focus in the same handler: to the next chip's remove button, or to the field the chips belong to.
dont: Leaving focus where it was. The focused element is about to be removed, and focus falls to `<body>`.
Asking for confirmation. Removing a chip is undone by adding the value back; a dialog for that is friction with no safety in it.
onRemove.a11y: The caller owns where focus goes next — see the decision on focus after removal.

removeLabel.summary: The remove button's full accessible name.
use: A translated phrase, in whatever word order the language needs: `removeLabel={t("remove", { name })}`.
dont: A bare 'Remove' or '×'. It must name the value, or every chip's button sounds the same.
removeLabel.a11y: Becomes the button's `aria-label`, and on native the label of the `delete` accessibility action.

icon.summary: A glyph before the text that says what kind of value it is.
use: A mail glyph on an address that is not a known contact, beside chips that are.
dont: The same glyph on every chip in a set. If it does not distinguish anything it is noise.
icon.a11y: Decorative — `aria-hidden`. If the kind of value matters, say it in the text.

disabled.summary: Blocks removal while keeping the button focusable and announced.
use: A value the reader cannot remove right now — a required recipient, a filter locked by a permission.
dont: A value that can never be removed. That is a Badge.
disabled.a11y: `aria-disabled` on the remove button, not the `disabled` attribute, so it stays in the tab order and is announced as unavailable.

className.summary: Extra classes, for placement — not for restyling it.
use: Rare. A set of chips gets its gap from the list that holds them.
dont: A status colour to mark an invalid value. Invalid input is a Field's message, and a red chip with no words says only 'something is wrong'.

usage.when: A set of values the reader built up and may trim.
usage.example:
{recipients.map((person, i) => (
  • removeRecipient(i)}>{person.name}
    • ))}
usage.notes: Each button is named 'Remove <name>'. `removeRecipient` must move focus to the next chip's button, or to the To field when the last chip goes — the component cannot, because it does not know what comes after it.

usage.case: The active filters above a result list
usage.when: Filters chosen elsewhere — in a Sheet of options — shown as a summary the reader can clear one by one.
usage.example: <Chip onRemove={() => clearFilter("colour")} removeLabel="Clear colour filter: Blue">Blue</Chip>
usage.notes: This is the removable summary of a filter, not the filter control. The control that sets it — a row of toggles — is ToggleButtonGroup with `selectionMode="multiple"`.

usage.case: Reaching for the wrong component: a filter toggle
usage.when: A row of options above a list, each turning a filter on or off in place.
usage.notes: Don't. A filter that toggles in place is pressed or not pressed, and that is ToggleButtonGroup with `selectionMode="multiple"` and `attached={false}`, which announces `aria-pressed`. An empty `onRemove` is the giveaway — there is nothing to remove.

usage.case: Reaching for the wrong component: a status label
usage.when: A label on a record that says what state it is in.
usage.notes: Don't. Nobody removes 'Paid' from an invoice by pressing an ×. That is a Badge, with `variant="success"`.
